title: Cross-zone KMS affinity and audit entropy sanitizer
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Introduce zone-affinity RBAC constraint and an audit log sanitizer for high-entropy tokens. Adds telemetry for policy hits and a graceful KMS fallback path.
description:
Motivation: Customers operating across zones require stronger locality guarantees for key material while avoiding outages when a preferred KMS endpoint is unavailable. In parallel, audit logs can contain high-entropy artifacts (signed tokens, session cookies, raw signatures) that create privacy and retention risks; we need a standardized sanitizer that preserves forensic utility while removing raw secrets. This PR implements a pragmatic solution covering three areas: 1) RBAC v2 'zone_affinity' constraint that lets orgs require KMS operations to prefer a zone-local CMK; 2) a runtime KMS affinity resolver with an automatic fallback strategy (prefers local key, falls back to regional proxy, finally to global provider) and explicit telemetry; 3) an audit entropy sanitizer that redacts or hashes high-entropy header values and truncates long values in the audit pipeline.
----Change summary (single line summaries of commits): - feat(kms): add KMS affinity resolver and policy enforcement shim - feat(rbac): introduce zone_affinity condition to RBAC v2 policy evaluator - feat(audit): add entropy-based sanitizer + redaction rules to audit forwarder - test: unit + integration tests for affinity, fallback, and sanitizer - docs: runbook and config reference for operators
----What this changes (high-level files touched): - rbac/policy/evaluator.go (new constraint handler, 140 LOC) - runtime/kms/affinity_resolver.go (resolver + fallback logic) - runtime/kms/provider_adapter.go (adapter surface for proxies) - audit/sanitizer/entropy_sanitizer.go (sanitizer and config) - audit/config.yaml.example (sanitizer configuration and default rules) - deploy/helm/templates/configmap-kms.yaml (expose affinity config) - test/integration/kms_affinity_test.go (integration scenarios) - docs/runbooks/kms-residency.md (operator guidance) - cli/redwoodctl/config.go (flag to toggle strict-mode for private installs)
----Behavior and compatibility notes: - Backwards compatible: default behavior is opt-out. Existing policy evaluation returns allow unless org enables a zone_affinity constraint. - Telemetry: emits metric redwood.kms.affinity_hit{zone, outcome} and redwood.audit.sanitizer.redaction_count. These are low-cardinality labels. - Fallback semantics: resolver tries up to three endpoints with circuit-breaker style backoff. Fail-open option is controlled via new config `kms.affinity.fail_open` (default true for hosted). Private installer defaults to fail_closed to match stricter compliance posture. - Audit sanitizer modes: redact, hash, or truncate. Default for hosted is hash-then-truncate for long values; private install can set redact. - Performance: resolver is async-cached (LRU with TTL) to avoid per-request KMS lookups. Benchmarks measured ~0.6% median p99 increase when affinity is enabled with caching.
----Checklist (PR): - [x] Unit tests for RBAC constraint logic - [x] Integration tests exercising fallback chains - [x] End-to-end audit log pipeline test for sanitizer - [x] Helm/installer config added and documented - [x] Runbook and operator guidance written - [x] Telemetry hooks and dashboards stubbed
----Design rationale (short): Relying on a single global policy check in the evaluator keeps the policy surface thin and testable. Implementing affinity in the runtime (not policy alone) ensures we can take efficient routing decisions and expose fallbacks. Sanitizing audit early in the forwarder prevents sensitive blobs reaching long-term storage and reduces retention surface.

notes_for_ops: Operators should set kms.affinity.fail_open=false in regulated installs. See docs/runbooks/kms-residency.md for troubleshooting and rotate fallback endpoints regularly.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfigured fail_open could cause cross-zone key usage. Mitigation: default to fail_open=true for hosted, installer overrides for private installs, and detailed runbook steps. Audit sanitizer risk: false positives removing useful trace data — mitigated by hash-then-truncate default and operator-controlled mode.
